title: NC early voting tops 2 million ballots ahead of Election Day - ABC11 News

 North Carolina early voting tops 2 million as voters cite economy, health care concerns 
 More than 2 million North Carolinians cast ballots during early voting ahead of Election Day. By Bianca Holman Saturday, October 31, 2026 10:38PM Share RALEIGH, N.C. (WTVD) -- More than 2 million North Carolinians had cast ballots as of Friday as early voting wrapped up Saturday ahead of the midterm election .
 The total represents just over 23% of statewide turnout . This election cycle is also surpassing early voting turnout at the same point four years ago.
 Across Raleigh, voters said issues ranging from the economy and inflation to taxes and health care were driving them to the polls.
 Raleigh resident Karen Bartolotta said Medicare, taxes and dental care were among the issues on her mind when casting her ballot.
 "Just Medicare issues and things like that," Bartolotta said.
 For Raleigh resident Shane Reid, the economy was a top concern.
 "The economy. You know, gas prices," Reid said. "It feels like we've been in inflation for forever now."
 Jason Tyson with the North Carolina State Board of Elections said turnout typically picks up at both ends of the early voting period.
 "Typically in elections, there's a surge at the beginning and there's a surge at the end of the early voting period," Tyson said.

 North Carolina's growing population is also contributing to higher voting numbers. Tyson said early voting is up 36% compared with 2020, while absentee voting has declined as voting habits have changed.
 Reid said he hopes the results of the midterm elections ultimately provide some economic relief, particularly as he begins thinking about retirement.
 "My dollar needs to go as far as it can go, because you can't really save for anything," Reid said. "I'm getting up in age now where I have to start thinking about retirement."
 Regardless of which candidates win, Reid said he wants Republicans and Democrats to work together.
 "Even if you do have Republicans in office and you got Democrats in the office, we got to work together because we're the ones that's going to suffer if they don't come together and work together," Reid said.
